claims.text: The patient presented with severe left knee pain and functional limitation due to end-stage osteoarthritis, characterized by a constant dull ache with episodes of sharp pain on weight-bearing, rated 8/10 to 9/10, present daily and worse in the mornings and after prolonged activity.
The patient reported occasional swelling and stiffness of the left knee joint but denied redness, fever, or systemic symptoms.
Past medical history includes end-stage osteoarthritis of the left knee with no other significant conditions.
Family history is positive for type 2 diabetes in the mother and hypertension in the father, with no family history of osteoarthritis or other joint disorders.

Social history indicates the patient lives with parents, is independent in activities of daily living but requires assistance for prolonged walking or standing, is a non-smoker, consumes approximately 4 units of alcohol per week, and has no recreational drug use.

Initial examination on 2025-12-20 revealed significant joint deformity with valgus alignment, tenderness along the medial joint line, reduced range of motion with pain on flexion beyond 70 degrees, and mild effusion in the left knee, with no signs of erythema, warmth, or active infection.
Initial vital signs on 2025-12-20 were heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 br/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO2 98%.

Initial investigations on 2025-12-20 showed mild anaemia with haemoglobin 11.3 g/dL, normal white cell count and platelets, normal urea and electrolytes, normal liver function tests, normal CRP, normal urinalysis, and a normal ECG with sinus rhythm.
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg once daily was prescribed on 2025-12-20 to address mild anaemia, with advice to increase dietary intake of iron-rich foods.

Anaesthetic assessment on 2025-12-20 confirmed an ASA grade of I, with a Mallampati score of I, adequate mouth opening, normal thyromental distance, and no history of respiratory disease or anaesthetic complications in the family.
Vital signs during anaesthetic assessment on 2025-12-20 were heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, with dual heart sounds and no murmurs.
Pre-operative instructions included a carbohydrate loading regimen to begin the day prior to surgery and fasting from midnight prior to the procedure.
On 2025-12-21, the patient provided formal written consent for total left knee replacement after discussion of benefits and risks, including infection, thromboembolism, and neurovascular injury.
Pre-operative assessment on 2025-12-21 showed heart rate 76 bpm, blood pressure 120/7 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, afebrile status, BMI 24, and no signs of infection.
Pre-operative checklist on 2025-12-21 confirmed fitness for surgery, absence of allergies, understanding of fasting instructions, and no current medications other than the prescribed ferrous sulfate.

On admission on 2026-01-05, examination showed the patient alert and cooperative with no distress, dual heart sounds, no murmurs, palpable symmetrical peripheral pulses, no peripheral oedema, and clear chest to auscultation.
Admission vital signs on 2026-01-05 were heart rate 74 bpm, blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 14 br/min, temperature 36.7°C, and SpO2 98% on room air.

Admission investigations on 2026-01-05 confirmed haemoglobin 11.3 g/dL, with other recent blood tests and urinalysis from 2025-12-20 remaining normal; a repeat haemoglobin level was requested and awaited.
Pre-surgical checklist on 2026-01-05 confirmed fasting compliance, verified consent, correct surgical site marking, and readiness for transfer to theatre.

Total left knee replacement was performed on 2026-01-05 under general anaesthesia, revealing severe cartilage degeneration and subchondral bone exposure with no peri-articular inflammation or infection.
A cemented total knee prosthesis was implanted with minimal estimated blood loss and no complications; the wound was closed with absorbable sutures and a sterile dressing.
Cefuroxime 1.5g IV was administered intra-operatively as prophylaxis.
Post-operative care plan included Tinzaparin 4,500 units subcutaneously once daily for thromboprophylaxis starting the evening of 2026-01-05, and Paracetamol 1g orally QDS PRN for pain.

Upon transfer to the PACU at 12:15 on 2026-01-05, the patient was drowsy but rousable, with stable vital signs, receiving 2L/min oxygen via nasal cannula, and a PCA pump with IV morphine 2 mg was initiated for pain management.
Surgical site inspection in the PACU showed no bleeding or swelling, with the sterile dressing intact and wound closed with absorbable sutures.
On 2026-01-05, the patient reported moderate pain at rest (6/10) and increased discomfort with movement, with the surgical site clean, minimal serous drainage, and no signs of infection.
Vital signs on 2026-01-05 ward round were heart rate 2 bpm, blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 1 br/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO2 98%.

Examination on 2026-01-05 showed the patient alert and oriented, with the left knee tender on palpation, limited movement secondary to pain, no calf tenderness or swelling, and no neurovascular deficits in the left lower limb.

On 2026-01-05, the plan was to start Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for thromboprophylaxis, prescribe Paracetamol 1g every 6 hours regularly, and prescribe Codeine phosphate 30 mg PRN for breakthrough pain.

Initial physiotherapy on 2026-01-06 focused on gentle mobilisation, with the patient achieving 40 degrees of flexion with mild discomfort (VAS 4/10) and performing deep breathing exercises without dizziness or shortness of breath.
Vital signs during physiotherapy on 2026-01-06 were heart rate 78 bpm, blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, SpO2 98% on room air, with the wound dressing intact and minimal serous drainage.
Physiotherapy plan on 2026-01-06 included independent continuation of exercises twice daily and progression to assisted walking exercises the following day.
The GP was contacted on 2026-01-06 to provide an update on post-operative progress, with anticipated discharge planned for 2026-01-09.
On 2026-01-06, the patient reported mild pain well controlled with oral analgesia, with the surgical site clean and dry, no erythema, swelling, or discharge, and no signs of DVT.
Vital signs on 2026-01-06 were heart rate 78 bpm, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 br/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO2 98% on room air.
Plan on 2026-01-06 included continuing Enoxaparin 40 mg SC OD for thromboprophylaxis until discharge, maintaining the current pain management plan, and continuing mobilisation with physiotherapy.

Physiotherapy on 2026-01-07 involved walking a short distance with a Zimmer frame and assisted knee flexion and extension exercises, with the patient reporting mild discomfort (3/10) and tolerating the session well.

Vital signs during physiotherapy on 2026-01-07 were heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, with the wound clean, dry, and no erythema or swelling.
Physiotherapy plan on 2026-01-07 included progression to crutches in the next session with a focus on stair navigation and continuing independent knee exercises twice daily.
Pharmacist review on 2026-01-07 recommended switching IV paracetamol to oral 1g QDS and continuing Ibuprofen 400mg TDS if tolerated.

Occupational therapy on 2026-01-07 assessed the patient's ability to perform ADLs, noting good balance with verbal prompts but requiring guidance to protect the operated knee, with recommendations for a raised toilet seat and sock aid.
On 2026-01-07, the patient reported manageable pain, improved mobility with a walking frame, and a haemoglobin level of 108 g/L indicating mild post-operative anaemia.
Vital signs on 2026-01-07 were heart rate 82 bpm, blood pressure 125/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 br/min, temperature 36.7°C, and SpO2 97% on room air.
Plan on 2026-01-07 included continuing physiotherapy, prescribing Ferrous sulfate 200 mg BD for post-operative anaemia, and transitioning to oral Ibuprofen 400 mg TDS for pain management.
On 2026-01-08, the patient reported satisfactory pain control and was mobilising well with a Zimmer frame, with a haemoglobin level of 108 g/L and no evidence of infection or further blood loss.
Vital signs on 2026-01-08 were heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 br/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO2 98% on room air.
Plan on 2026-01-08 included switching regular paracetamol to PRN dosing, prescribing Co-amoxiclav 500/125 mg TDS for 7 days for wound infection prophylaxis, and continuing Ferrous sulfate 200 mg BD.

Final physiotherapy session on 2026-01-08 focused on safe use of crutches for independent mobilisation, including walking on flat surfaces and navigating stairs, with the patient deemed safe for discharge with crutches.
Vital signs during final physiotherapy on 2026-01-08 were heart rate 72 bpm, blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, SpO2 97% on room air, with the surgical wound clean, dry, and no erythema or swelling.

Discharge instructions on 2026-01-08 included detailed wound care, a pain management plan of oral Paracetamol 1g QDS and Ibuprofen 400mg TDS, and a follow-up appointment scheduled for 2026-01-15 with the GP.

Occupational therapy review on 2026-01-08 confirmed the patient demonstrated independence and safety in bed transfers, crutch use on stairs, and household tasks, with discharge planned for the following day.
